_comment: BYS360 coverage ratchet baseline. Truthful, re-measured floor for CI's actual test scope (tests/quality -m ci_safe, then tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services, branch=true). This value is NOT aspirational and must NEVER be raised automatically by any script -- raising it is a separate, human-reviewed action after real coverage genuinely improves. See scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py for enforcement logic and its docstring for the no-self-raise constraint.
_history: Phase 6 CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure (2026-07-27): tests/services (422 tests) was added to the CI-enforced coverage scope -- it was previously excluded for no remaining technical reason (root cause: a stalled Campaign-1 rollout plan, not flakiness/perf/DB-dependency; verified via 3 stability runs, 0 skip/xfail/realdb/slow/live markers, no dedicated conftest.py). Combined coverage measured twice, identically, at 23.2735%. Previous baseline (CI scope without tests/services, Campaign 1B, 2026-07-24) was combined_pct=18.85 -- kept here for continuity, not reused as the active floor.
measured_by: BYS360 Phase 6 - CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure

previous_baseline.scope: tests/quality (ci_safe) + tests/integration + tests/architecture + tests/security + tests/critical (tests/services NOT included)

environment.os: Windows 11 (worktree measurement; CI runner is ubuntu-latest -- see tolerance note in ratchet script)

commands: python -m pytest tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services --cov=app --cov-append --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml:reports/quality/coverage.xml --cov-fail-under=0 --tb=short -q

repeatability.note: Two independent full runs of the new combined command produced an identical measurement (deterministic given no test randomization is in use). The recorded combined_pct is the true measured value, consistent with lines_covered/lines_valid/branches_covered/branches_valid (see tests/quality/test_bys360_coverage_ratchet.py::test_committed_baseline_counts_are_internally_consistent); the sole safety margin is the pre-existing tolerance_pct field below, unchanged at 0.5 points.

tolerance_rationale: Absorbs float rounding and Windows-worktree-vs-Ubuntu-CI-runner platform noise (this baseline was measured on Windows; the actual CI runner is ubuntu-latest, which can take slightly different code paths on OS-conditional branches). Not intended to absorb a real coverage regression, which is expected to be much larger than 0.5 points in practice.
